ideas.title: Is he lying? You've got three seconds.
ideas.body: Close-up of a player placing their bid. Freeze the frame, three-second countdown, then the cup comes up. The viewer plays the game inside the feed instead of watching it, and the comments fill with people claiming they knew.

ideas.title: 3 signs your game night is dying, even though everyone showed up.
ideas.body: Phones out. Someone explaining rules for twenty minutes. One person thinking for four minutes while the rest stare at the ceiling. Then the turn: teaches in 90 seconds, almost no downtime, 40-60 minutes.

ideas.title: You already know how to play this. You just don't know it yet.
ideas.body: Liar's Dice is 70 percent of the game. The rest is the race around the map. Removes the barrier for anyone who assumes a premium box means a thick rulebook.

ideas.title: The dishwasher is older than the airplane.
ideas.body: Dishwasher 1886, airplane 1903, both from our own deck. Two cards face down, three seconds to guess, then flip. People cannot resist arguing about it in the comments.

ideas.title: I gave the same three cards to a 9-year-old and a 40-year-old.
ideas.body: The selfie stick is from 1983. Both guess wrong, the kid wins. Sells exactly what makes it a gift: age 8 and up, but adults lose.

ideas.title: Fifteen seconds of Blitz. History games aren't slow.
ideas.body: No turns, everyone places at once, hands everywhere, someone shouts. Kills the objection that a game about dates sounds like homework.
